neighbours.label: the punctuation ('?', '…', '.') right after a one-word reply or interjection that opens a line of dialogue (Really? Yes? Yeah… Okay.), as against the same punctuation closing a full sentence
fire: She looked up from her book. "Seriously? You lost the keys again?"
A voice called from the hall: "Hello? Is anyone in the kitchen?"
He shrugged. "Well… I guess we could try."
She nodded slowly. "Okay. Then we leave at six."
The clerk leaned closer. "Sorry? I didn't catch your name."
He rubbed his chin. "Maybe… but I doubt it will work."
She spun around. "What? Who told you that?"
He threw up his hands. "Fine. Do it your way."
quiet: She looked up from her book. "Did you really lose the keys again?"
A voice called from the hall to ask whether anyone was in the kitchen.
He shrugged and said that they could try it tomorrow.
She nodded slowly. "We are going to leave the house at six."
The clerk leaned closer. "I am afraid I did not catch your name."
He rubbed his chin. "I doubt that the new plan will work at all."
She spun around. "Who was the person who told you about that?"
He threw up his hands. "You can do the whole thing your own way."
